entries.verificationTarget: CTS requests GR2K923484, GR2K923501, GR2K923503, GR2K923525, GR2K923527 and GR2K923531 on w200/client 200, called for real on 2026-10-01; every request-level release reached the physical export and SAP answered TRANSPORT_EXPORT_FAILED with its own text '无法启动传输控制程序 tp', leaving E070 TRSTATUS at D and releasing nothing
entries.notes: RULED THE PLATFORM BOUNDARY BY THE OPERATOR ON 2026-10-01, after the cause was read out of SAP's own source rather than inferred. The tool is NOT deleted and does NOT pretend to work: it still refuses honestly, refusing an already-released request with TRANSPORT_NOT_MODIFIABLE and reporting the callee's own TRANSPORT_EXPORT_FAILED otherwise. What is ruled out of reach is one link, and the evidence for it is complete. (1) THE EXPORT CANNOT BE SKIPPED. FORM TRINT_RELEASE_REQUEST (137 lines, sha256 931d02ad...), second step, branches only on trfunction and on whether a target system is present: 'IF trfunction CA sctsc_types_tasks', 'ELSEIF customizing AND strkorr <> space', 'ELSEIF (customizing OR workbench) AND tarsystem = space' each emit a message and export nothing, and the ELSE branch calls TRINT_TRANSPORT_REQUEST. A workbench (K) request WITH a target - which is exactly what this service creates, TARSYSTEM = GR3 - always falls into ELSE. There is no caller-selectable input that avoids this: TRINT_TRANSPORT_REQUEST (106 lines, sha256 46690e87...) calls TRINT_EXPORT_ON_OS_LEVEL unconditionally, with no IF around it, and then maps sy-subrc 2/4 to export_failed; and TRINT_EXPORT_ON_OS_LEVEL's interface (LSCTS_RELEASE$02, sha256 88dfa526...) accepts only IV_TRKORR, IV_TARGET, IT_E071, IV_DIALOG, IV_CALLED_BY_PERFORCE and IV_DISPLAY_EXPORT_LOG - IV_DIALOG selects dialog versus background behaviour of the export, not whether it happens. An earlier hypothesis of this project, that the SE09 dialog reaches a released status by some branch that skips the export, is therefore WRONG and is withdrawn: the dialog runs the same export. (2) THAT EXPORT NEEDS THE OS-LEVEL tp. The chain continues LSCTS_RELEASEF02 FORM release_by_tp (line 21) -> 'PERFORM tp_interface USING lv_trkorr space 'EXPWBO' 'X'' (line 49) -> TMS_TP_EXPORT. The refusal text is the callee's own, so the missing piece is an operating-system program, not a SAP object. (3) tp IS NOT REACHABLE IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. tp exists as an AIX executable at /usr/sap/GR2/SYS/exe/run/tp (17,305,532 bytes, owner gr2adm, mtime 2014-05-12 17:34:47) and belongs to a coherent 2014-05-12 kernel set, so it was not singled out or removed; the TMS domain configuration is present (/usr/sap/trans/bin holds DOMAIN.CFG and TP_DOMAIN_GR2.PFL) and /usr/sap/trans/data and /cofiles hold real export artefacts. What the readings do show is that no transport log has been written since 2014-02-02 (SLOG1351.GR4 and ALOG1351.GR4 are the newest), and that a genuine release performed by the operator on 2026-10-01 moved GR2K923527 to TRSTATUS = R WITHOUT writing any SLOG/ALOG and WITHOUT producing new R*/K* files. E070 status alone is therefore not evidence that tp ran - an inference this project had made and has now positively refuted. Repairing this is operating-system and TMS work on an AIX application server: it needs root or gr2adm on the host and S_CTS_ADMI in STMS, and the operator has stated they are not a Basis administrator and have no OS access. The capability is therefore not deliverable in this environment. (4) THIS IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A CLEARED HOLE. The same reasoning was already accepted for the sibling tool in this family, cleanup_transport_entries, which is registered platform-unsupported for the analogous reason that native ADT removeobject is absent on ECC 7.31 SP04. The family's gap text states the boundary explicitly rather than being emptied, so nothing here claims a verification that did not happen. WHAT WAS PROVEN ALONG THE WAY, and stays true: the task-level arm does release for real (task GR2K923528 reached TRSTATUS = R, this project's first genuine release), add_objects_to_transport writes for real (insertedCount = 1), and three real call-site defects were found, fixed, deployed and proven on the machine - the ET_MESSAGES by-reference export passed under EXPORTING instead of IMPORTING (short dump CALL_FUNCTION_PARM_UNKNOWN before any release logic ran), iv_as_background_job = 'X' selecting the release_in_bg_mode branch (LSCTS_RELEASEF13:848) that never releases, and the request being released before its tasks. Four alternative explanations were each falsified by evidence first: a stale application-server buffer; the CTS project/serialization check; 'tp is not runnable at all'; and 'E071-LOCKFLAG = X means the object is still locked' - the last refuted by request GR2K900281, which reached TRSTATUS = R while carrying LOCKFLAG = X rows, and by this request's own LOCKFLAG moving from X to 3 when it was released. Every attempt was a safe failure: E070 stayed D and GR2K923472 was never touched. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS: a repaired tp environment (tp executable permission, TMS domain profile, transport directory write access on the AIX host) would let a single genuine request-level release succeed, at which point this entry should be re-verified and promoted, not left at the boundary.

entries.verificationTarget: w200 through the repo-dist instance on port 4849 on 2026-09-29 15:26, after the 2.18 helper body landed: four real calls over GR2K918001 (E070 status R, target GR3, released 2020-09-02), GR2K923472 (status D), GR2K999999 (absent) and AAAK000001 (absent)
entries.notes: NOT PROVEN, named first: seven of the nine verdicts the arm can return were never observed. The importable answer (callee sub-return code 0) has never run on w200 - every request tried was refused - so the positive branch is documented, not demonstrated, and neither were permission_denied, import_not_allowed, tp_call_failed, tp_interface_error, tp_reported_error or tp_reported_info; only enqueue_failed (3) and the service-side input refusal were exercised. Nor was the undeclared-exception failure path (sub-return code 99) or the tool's 2.18 floor against a 2.17 helper, since only one repository helper exists here. What WAS verified: after the 2.18 body landed (sourceHash e8b6386569ad6a521d48a440370deedc396bbc4faf22dadce6ca72b9dece761e, identical to the export sha256) four real calls returned status ok, code TRANSPORT_IMPORT_CHECKED, verdict enqueue_failed, calleeSubrc 3, importable false, the request echoed and LOCAL_E070_STATUS correct for each - R for GR2K918001, D for GR2K923472, not-found for the two absent numbers - so a refusal is an answer and every field is attributable. That is the correction of a measured defect: the 2.17 arm translated the callee's exception number into a meaning (1 into no-authority, 2 into not-allowed) and dropped every payload row when it reported a failure, and nine real calls on the same day showed the translation was wrong in both directions - a failed tp start was labelled a refusal and a refusal was labelled a failure - with GR2K918001 returning not-allowed at 14:51 and TRANSPORT_IMPORT_CHECK_FAILED from 14:53 on, and AAAK000001 likewise minutes apart. The 2.18 arm reports the callee's own exception name and the raw sub-return code on every path, so the reply is mechanical rather than interpretive; the service validates the verdict against the arm's closed vocabulary, exposes calleeSubrc, and treats a success reply without it as TRANSPORT_RESPONSE_INVALID. Not established and recorded as a risk rather than settled: whether the callee's simulate mode starts a tp process. Its own messages name tp, so the earlier claim that it exits before the tp call is not supported by observation, and the read channel could not settle it - TPSTAT is refused by the D5-2 allowlist, read_file_system_directory on /usr/sap/trans/log reported the kernel file counter at 78063 against zero DIR_LIST rows, and /usr/sap/trans failed with RUNTIME_RESOURCES_RFC_FAILED. Also unresolved: helperMessage is rendered from sy-msg*, which CALL FUNCTION ... EXCEPTIONS does not clear, so a message-less exception could in theory surface the previous call's text; the whole helper uses that same pattern and calleeSubrc is the authoritative discriminator. The callee's message is generic and not a statement about the request - two absent request numbers were told their import had already run - so it must not be read as evidence that any request was imported. The transport family does not close on this promotion: release_transport_task is still unverified by the operator's own deferral.
